headline: TCSD Reviews Budget, Approves Personnel and Policy Updates Ahead of School Year
summary: At its annual budget hearing and a special called meeting, the board reviewed the district's budget outlook and approved personnel, fundraisers, facility-use requests, three policy revisions and purchases including 10 school buses and a TCHS video surveillance system. A special meeting was scheduled for July 31 to approve the budget.

personnel.note: Hires include 4 substitute teachers, 2 homebound teachers, a computer lab assistant, an assistant girls' basketball coach and a certified special education teacher; other = 2 volunteer coaches; 1 personnel transfer listed. National Board supplements for 2 teachers are listed under money.

money.item: Fiber installation at Belmont Baseball Field House
Terminate/configure and finish fiber installation to Belmont Baseball Field House
Stamp machine rental agreement (state contract price), Belmont School, 48 months
Contract campus cleanup services at TCHS
Fence replacement at TCHS football field
Annual fire extinguisher inspection agreements, district-wide
National Board supplements for 2 teachers (pending state funds)

policy.item: Cell phone/electronic device policy: use allowed after the 'last dismissal bell' instead of 'after 3:30'.
Tobacco policy: students found violating the policy with THC/synthetics to be referred to Youth Court.
Drugs/alcohol policy: drug detection canines to visit each campus at least two times per semester.

superintendent: Superintendent Christie Holly informed the board of New Teacher Orientation on July 23 and Opening Day Convocation at Belmont on July 28.
A special board meeting was scheduled for July 31 at 8:00 a.m. to approve the budget; students return Friday, Aug. 1, 2025.
otherActions: Budget hearing: the State has instructed districts to prepare for reduced federal funding
Budget hearing: previously approved adult meal price increases for 2025-2026 were addressed (breakfast $2.25 to $2.40; lunch $4.00 to $4.10)

Budget hearing: district overview - 2,788 students (2024-25); about 477 full-time staff projected (2025-26); 96 buildings, about 696,000 sq ft; 48 bus routes, over 465,000 miles a year; over 140,000 breakfasts and 450,000 lunches served (2024-25)
